messages:
alice: hey @support — since ~09:10 PDT our requests to /v1/generate are spiking 500s and timeouts. saw ~30% error rate and p95 latency jumped to 3s. example req id: req_9a8b. can you help?

sarah: sorry about that — we're looking. can you paste a sample request (headers + minimal body) and the request id? any host region?
alice: us-west-2. sample curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-EX\" -d '{\"prompt\":\"test\",\"max_tokens\":64}'`
response: `HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout` and body `{"error":"upstream timeout"}`. req id repeated for different calls: req_9a8b, req_9a9c, req_9ad2.

sarah: thx. tagging infra/sre & runtime. @devon @oliver can you take a look?
devon: on it. initial look at proxy logs shows a bunch of `502` and `upstream read timeout` from the backend; also seeing `cache lookup error` lines. pulling cache metrics now.
devon: metrics: redis-cache cluster `prefix-cache-usw2` P99 command latency jumped to 1.2s, connection errors increased, and connection pool saturation = true. memcached fallback also showing increased miss/latency. looks like KV/prefix cache is overloaded.
oliver: vouched — runtime side shows `KV_PREFIX_GET` ops timing out, then downstream model containers queue up and hit gateway timeouts. stack snippet from runtime logs:
```
[2026-03-15T16:10:42Z] ERROR kv_client.go:142 timeout getting key prefix: ctx deadline exceeded key=prefix:session:abcd
[2026-03-15T16:10:43Z] WARN proxy.go:88 upstream read timeout -> returning 504
[2026-03-15T16:10:44Z] ERROR redis-pool.go:67 connection refused or timeout (pool exhausted)
```

oliver: looks like the prefix cache dependency (redis/memcached) is the critical path. when the cache blocks, we don't have a graceful bypass and requests pile up.

marcus: oncall alerted. initial mitigation options: 1) scale cache cluster (add nodes), 2) toggle prefix-caching feature off for hosted inference traffic to fallback to cold reads, 3) increase cache connection pool/timeouts to avoid blocking system threads.
sarah: which is fastest to reduce 5xx for customers?
devon: immediate: toggle prefix caching off for the affected region (us-west-2) via FF so runtime does cold KV lookup (slower per-request cost but avoids 5xx). medium: scale cluster and replenish nodes. long: add async fallback + circuit breaker into runtime.

oliver: I can flip FF `runtime.prefix_cache.enabled` -> `false` for canary and monitor. will do a canary on 5% of traffic then 100% if green.

sarah: please also notify customers impacted and put an incident page.

oliver: deploy-bot: starting feature-flag rollout `runtime.prefix_cache.enabled=false` canary 5% us-west-2
deploy-bot: canary done — observing metrics (5%): error rate down from 32% -> 8% for canary buckets :eyes:

oliver: rolling to 100% for us-west-2 now
deploy-bot: rollout complete 100% us-west-2 at 16:23 UTC :rocket:

oliver: post-rollout checks: p95 latency back to ~220ms, error rate down to 2-3%. CPU on model nodes normalized. KV cache metrics show reduced client-side timeouts (because we bypassed the cache).

sarah: thanks — reaching out to alice with update.
sarah: @alice we have a mitigation in place (disabled prefix caching in us-west-2). you should see errors go away; can you confirm?
alice: testing now — on first quick run errors dropped significantly, p95 back to ~250ms — looks good. we'll keep monitoring for 15m and report if anything pops. thanks.
devon: logging root-cause ticket: `INC-1234` — provisional cause: cache node memory pressure + sudden spike in unique prefixes causing high eviction and connection pool starvation on prefix-cache-usw2.
devon: repro steps for engineering investigation:
1) hit /v1/generate with 200 concurrent clients from us-west-2 with varying long prompts to produce many unique prefix keys.
2) observe `prefix-cache-usw2` client metrics: connection pool saturates and `ctx deadline exceeded` appears in runtime logs.
3) run `redis-cli --latency -h redis-prefix-1.usw2.internal` during test and note P99.

oliver: quick mitigation on infra side — scaling cache nodes + bumping `maxclients` on memcached cluster. infra is provisioning + should be ready in ~40m.

marcus: created incident page https://infra.redwood/status/INC-1234 and set priority P1. added postmortem owner @devon.

sarah: summary for support follow-up: 1) root cause probably cache eviction/connection pool exhaustion on prefix cache. 2) mitigation: toggled `runtime.prefix_cache.enabled=false` for us-west-2 and scaling cache cluster. 3) next steps: add circuit-breaker and async fallback to runtime, improve cache autoscaling, add better alerting on pool saturation.

alice: all good here for now. will reopen if we see anything. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

devon: leaving follow-up ticket to implement nonblocking bypass + circuit breaker; link: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INFRA-4556
sarah: closing thread when incident is stable. we’ll post postmortem once root cause fully confirmed.

sre-bot: incident INC-1234 acknowledged by oncall. timeline started at 2026-03-15T16:10:30Z.
